patch_description: The best prior program (sum 2.40) achieved its score via a randomized hill-climb over center positions with LP re-solves; the current program dropped that search, losing performance (2.36). I restore the hill-climb but improve it per the recommendation: instead of isotropic Gaussian steps, each move perturbs a circle along its "slack" direction — the direction of maximum available space (away from its nearest blocking wall or neighbor) — blended with a small random component. This raises acceptance probability of each LP re-solve, so the fixed time budget (~1.2s) yields more improvements. I also bias circle selection toward circles with small radii (they have the most slack to exploit). A lightweight non-LP score proxy (minimum pairwise/wall slack) lets us reject clearly-bad moves before paying the LP cost, further increasing effective throughput.
